text: Overconsumption of single use products have devastating consequences on our natural environment. Through the entire lifecycle of a product, disposable packaging and the products themselves unnecessarily consume resources, releasing harmful greenhouses gases and other toxins in the extraction, processing and manufacturing process. Following their brief use, much of this waste finds its way back into the natural environment as litter or trash that must be treated. According to Provincial recycling reports, plastics have the lowest recycling rate of all packaging and disposable products (only 29 percent of plastic packaging is recycled, compared to paper at 74 percent, glass at 73 percent, and metal at 53 percent). The Province is currently reviewing provincial waste regulations including packaging and recycling collection. The City would be well served to lead the way by proposing changes…
The Public Works and Infrastructure Committee: 1. Referred the item to the General Manager, Solid Waste Management Services for consideration as part of the Long Term Waste Management Strategy.
